🏆 Vendor of the Week

Tiled: When Design Becomes a Learning Advantage

How an interactive microapp platform is transforming our curriculum—and why we're running an A/B test to prove that great design actually drives better learning outcomes.

Anthony Brock sent me a link last month. No pitch deck, no intro email—just a URL. "Take a look," he wrote. "Tell me what you think."

I clicked through and realized I was looking at my own curriculum. Same introduction. Same Unit 1. Same frameworks I'd been refining for months. But it didn't feel like my curriculum. It felt like something you'd actually want to spend time with—smooth transitions, thoughtful animations, content that revealed itself as you scrolled rather than dumping everything on the page at once.

I'd built the Future of PMM on a standard web stack—HTML, JavaScript, Netlify. It worked. People learned from it. But Anthony had taken that same content and transformed it into something that made you forget you were "learning." You were just... exploring.

The result: s.tiled.co/2r9iip5/sap-curriculum

The welcome screen. Notice how different this feels from scrolling through documentation.

Tiled calls these "microapps"—interactive experiences built from your existing content. The term undersells it. What they've really built is a container that makes B2B content behave like consumer media. You know that feeling when you're three episodes into a Netflix show and realize you should have gone to bed an hour ago? That's what good design does. It removes the friction between you and the thing you're consuming.

The Pitch That Worked

I get a lot of vendor pitches. Most of them sound like this: "Our AI-powered platform enables seamless content transformation at scale." Delete.

Anthony Brock, Senior Manager at Tiled, tried something different. He didn't talk about the platform. He built the demo using my stuff—our actual curriculum, our actual frameworks, our actual brand. The pitch wasn't "imagine what this could do." The pitch was "look at what this already does."

Anthony Brock

Senior Manager, Enterprise Accounts · Tiled

Based in Lehi, Utah. Previously at Domo, Adobe, and Pluralsight. The guy who saw our curriculum and thought: this could be better if it felt better.

That instinct—that the vessel matters as much as the content—is exactly what product marketers are supposed to understand. We obsess over positioning and messaging and packaging. We'll spend weeks debating whether a slide deck tells a story or just dumps data. But when it comes to our own learning materials? PDFs. Static pages. The same formats we'd never accept for a customer-facing asset.

Anthony noticed the gap.

Tiled at a Glance

Does It Actually Work?

Pretty presentations are easy to dismiss. Eye candy. Sugar high. But Tiled's customer results suggest something more interesting is going on.

IBM reported a 250% increase in content engagement after switching their sales materials to Tiled microapps. Compass Canteen saw a 19% lift in conversion rates. These aren't "time on page" vanity metrics—they're measuring whether people actually do something after consuming the content. Click the next step. Book the meeting. Sign the contract.

"We use Tiled microapps to deepen relationships with our most important accounts. And what would have taken us weeks to create before Tiled, we can now create in a single afternoon."
— Ray Oram, VP of Marketing, IBM

Still—I'm skeptical by nature. Vendor case studies are curated. The successes get published; the failures get buried. So we're going to run our own experiment.

The 72% statistic that frames our "Point of View" section—visual hierarchy that draws the eye.

The A/B Test

We're not going to assert that the Tiled experience is better. We're going to prove it—or disprove it.

🧪 Our Experiment

Control: Standard futureofpmm.com curriculum (Intro + Unit 1)
Treatment: Tiled microapp version of the same content
Metrics: Completion rate, time on content, quiz scores, learner satisfaction
Reporting: Results published here in 4 weeks

Same content. Same assessment. Different container. If the Tiled version drives better outcomes, we roll it out across the full curriculum. If it doesn't, we've learned something important about where design matters and where it's just decoration.

Either way, we publish the results.

The AI Impact Matrix—same data, but with tabbed navigation and interactive exploration.
